reasons: Declared independent-unit column basin_id matches the frozen data: 10 rows, 10 distinct basin codes, each on exactly one row, with 5 distinct units in the rewetted arm and 5 in the drained arm and no unit shared across arms.

The selected report demonstrates absence of the issue: it states each basin contributes exactly one row measured once, identifies the basin as both randomisation unit and unit of analysis, and notes no basin is entered more than once.

The permutation reference set of 252 splits equals C(10,5) over the 10 unique basins, confirming one observation per independent unit in the enumeration; reported group counts (5 vs 5) match the data.
Reported statistics reproduce from the frozen data: rewetted mean 23.34, drained mean 16.94, contrast +6.40 mg/L, p = 16/252 = 0.0635, correctly described as not reaching the 0.05 level.
The workflow enforces uniqueness of basin codes with a hard error in read_basins, so duplicated units would abort rather than enter the row-independent procedure.
No authority lock was minted, so lock_follows_declaration is not-applicable-no-lock.

The declared independent-unit column plot_id is consistent with the frozen data: exactly 12 plot identifiers (PLOT-01 through PLOT-12) each appear in exactly 5 campaign rows, and each plot's treatment label is fixed across all its rows, yielding 6 biochar plots and 6 control plots, matching the data description for both procedure arms.

The selected report demonstrates the issue on its face: it states that 12 plots were visited in 5 campaigns, then that 'each chamber measurement was entered as one replicate observation of its treatment, giving 30 observations per treatment', and the selected result reports a Welch two-sample t-test on 60 chamber measurements with df = 55.8. This shows the five repeated measurements from each plot (the declared independent unit) were entered into a row-independent two-sample t-test as if they were 60 independent replicates, when there are only 12 independent units (6 per arm).

The workflow confirms the same: read_efflux pools every CSV row's co2_flux_umol_m2_s by treatment with no aggregation over plot_id before calling scipy.stats.ttest_ind, so within-plot dependence is ignored by the procedure.

The lock's unit-key authorization does not follow from the declaration alone: the declaration establishes that plot_id is the independent unit and that each plot_id recurs five times in the input, so row-level entries keyed by plot_id are not independent. Authorizing scipy.stats.ttest_ind — a procedure that treats each row as an independent observation — as dependence-free over this input with authorized_key_columns ['plot_id'] contradicts, rather than follows from, that declaration; the authorization would only follow if plot_id were unique per row or the data were first aggregated to one value per plot.

Declared independent-unit column stream_code is consistent with the frozen data: 24 rows with 24 unique codes (PG01-PG24), each row holding both the June and September measurement, and both arms of the paired comparison come from within the same row.

The report demonstrates absence of the repeated-measures-as-independent-rows issue: the paired visits are collapsed to one signed change per stream before testing, so the sign test's n (24) equals the number of independent catchments, not the 48 individual water samples.

The per-stream table lists each of the 24 stream codes exactly once with a delta that matches the frozen data (e.g., PG01: 2.63 - 2.14 = +0.49), and the counts recompute from it: 18 increases, 6 decreases (PG05, PG09, PG14, PG18, PG21, PG24), 0 ties.
The reported statistics verify against recomputation: proportion 18/24 = 0.750 and exact two-sided binomial p = 2 * 190051 / 2^24 ~= 0.0227, matching the selected result.
No authority lock was minted, so lock_follows_declaration is not-applicable-no-lock.

Declared independent-unit column module_id is consistent with the frozen data in both arms: six nanocoat modules (PV-C01..PV-C06) and six bare modules (PV-U01..PV-U06) each appear exactly five times (weeks 1-5), 60 rows total, with no module in both arms.

The selected report demonstrates the issue: it states the two-sample Student t-test was run 'with each of the 60 inspection records entered as one independent observation' and reports t(58), i.e., degrees of freedom from 60 rows rather than 12 independent modules.

The per-module table (5 inspections per module) and group summary (30 records per arm from only 6 modules each) in the report make the repeated-measures structure explicit, so the correlated rows entering scipy.stats.ttest_ind as independent is shown in the report itself, not merely inferable from the workflow.

The minted lock's authorized_key_columns ["module_id"] exactly matches the declared independent-unit column, so the unit-key authorization follows from the declaration alone; per its stated limitations the lock does not establish numerical impact or scientific correctness and does not cure the demonstrated dependence.

Declaration check: the declared independent-unit column digester_id is consistent with the frozen data. data/input.csv contains exactly 12 distinct digester_id values (DG01-DG12), each appearing exactly 4 times (run days 6, 10, 14, 18), and pretreatment is constant within every digester_id, giving 6 vessels in the control arm (DG01, DG03, DG05, DG08, DG09, DG12) and 6 in the thermal arm (DG02, DG04, DG06, DG07, DG10, DG11), matching the declaration for both procedure arms.

Selected report demonstration: the report demonstrates the ABSENCE of the repeated-measures-as-independent issue. It explicitly states the 48 records are repeated measurements nested within 12 vessels, tabulates one collapsed mean per digester (12 rows, each with 4 sessions), and runs the Mann-Whitney U test on the 12 vessel-level means (n = 6 vs 6), so each independent unit enters the row-independent procedure exactly once.

Numerical verification supports the demonstration: recomputed vessel means match the table (e.g., DG01 = (268.3+251.1+271.4+258.4)/4 = 262.3), control/thermal means of digester means are 257.17 and 301.15, medians 258.75 and 301.30 (gap 42.55), and complete separation of the 6-vs-6 vessel means yields U = 36.0 with exact two-sided p = 2/924 = 0.002165, exactly as reported. These statistics are only reachable from 12 vessel-level values, not 48 pooled session rows (which would give U up to 576).

Lock check: a lock is minted (dependence_method_authorization_v1) and its authorization follows from the declaration alone. authorized_key_columns is exactly ["digester_id"], identical to the declared independent-unit column with no additions or substitutions; the procedure record resolves to scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu, the row-independent procedure actually used on the per-unit values; authority_state is authorized by a human actor and the stated authority limitations correctly disclaim execution or correctness guarantees.

Declared independent-unit column shrub_id is consistent with the frozen data: 48 rows carry 12 distinct shrub IDs, 4 leaves per shrub, with 6 shrubs per cultivar arm (S01-S06 Catuai, S07-S12 Obata), so the unit key repeats within both procedure arms exactly as the data description states.

The selected report demonstrates the issue: it states every leaf measurement was entered as a single observation into Welch's two-sample t-test (a row-independent procedure), its table shows 24 leaf measurements versus only 6 shrubs sampled per cultivar, and it reports n = 24 per group with df = 44.17 explicitly derived from the 48 leaf rows — repeated measurements per shrub treated as independent.

The lock's unit-key authorization follows from the declaration alone: authorized_key_columns is ["shrub_id"], identical to the declared independent-unit column, and the lock's stated limitations confirm it asserts nothing beyond the case, input digest, procedure, and ordered key.
